references.text: Isaiah 9:1-2 predicts that the people who walked in darkness will see a great light, a direct counterpart to Jesus' call to believe in the light to become children of the light.
Isaiah 42:6 describes the Messiah as a light for the nations, which corresponds with the theme of believing in the light to become part of God's people.
In John 8:12, Jesus declares that he is the light of the world, and that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, a direct theological precursor to the call in 12:36.
John 1:4-5 establishes that life is the light for all people and that the light shines in the darkness, forming the basis for the call to believe in the light.
Ephesians 5:8 describes believers as once being darkness but now being light in the Lord, and urges them to walk as children of the light, a direct parallel to the result of believing in the light.

1 Peter 2:9 calls believers a chosen people who are to proclaim the praises of him who called them out of darkness into his wonderful light, a theme that reflects the identity of being children of the light.
